paras.text: The most important responsibility of the legislature is law-making. The constitution gives the legislature this responsibility of making laws on the list of federal subjects. The list of federal subjects (Federal Legislative List) is the list on whose subjects the National Assembly and Senate can make laws. paras.urdu: مقننہ کی سب سے اہم ذمہ داری قانون سازی کرنا ہے۔ آئین مقننہ کو یہ ذمہ داری دیتا ہے کہ وفاقی اُمور کی فہرست سے قانون سازی کرے۔ وفاقی اُمور کی فہرست (Federal Legislative List) وہ فہرست ہے جس میں دیئے گئے موضوعات پر قومی اسمبلی و سینٹ قانون بنا سکتی ہے۔ آئین کے مطابق اگر کسی ناخوشگوار صورتِ حال کی وجہ سے صدرِ مملکت کسی صوبے میں ہنگامی حالت (Emergency) کا نفاذ کرے تو صوبائی اسمبلی کی قانون سازی کا اختیار معطل ہو جاتا ہے اور اُس صوبے کیلئے قومی اسمبلی و سینٹ قانون سازی کرتی ہے۔ مرکزی اسمبلی کی غیر موجودگی میں صدرِ پاکستان کو حکم نامہ یا عارضی قانون (Ordinance) جاری کرنے کا اختیار ہے لیکن اگر قومی اسمبلی و سینٹ کا اجلاس شروع ہو جائے تو صدر کے حکم ناموں کو یا تو باقاعدہ قانونی شکل دی جاتی ہے یا اسے ختم کر دیئے جاتے ہیں۔ شمالی علاقوں اور وفاقی دارالحکومت اسلام آباد کیلئے قانون سازی کا حق قومی اسمبلی و سینٹ کو حاصل ہے۔ مقننہ سادہ اکثریت سے عام قانون کو ختم یا تبدیل کر سکتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: د مقننې تر ټولو مهم مسؤلیت قانون جوړول دي. اساسي قانون مقننې ته دا مسؤلیت ورکوي چې د فدرالي چارو له لړلیک قانون جوړ کړي. د فدرالي چارو لړلیک (Federal Legislative List) هغه لړلیک دی چې په ورکړل شویو موضوعاتو یې ملي شورا او سنا قانون جوړولی شي. د اساسي قانون له مخې که د کوم ناخوښه حالت له امله ولسمشر په کوم ولایت کې بیړنی حالت (Emergency) نافذ کړي، د ولایتي شورا د قانون جوړونې واک ځنډول کېږي او د هغه ولایت لپاره ملي شورا او سنا قانون جوړوي. د مرکزي شورا په نشتوالي کې د پاکستان ولسمشر ته د فرمان یا لنډمهاله قانون (Ordinance) د صادرولو واک دی، خو که د ملي شورا او سنا غونډه پیل شي، د ولسمشر فرمانونه یا منظم قانوني بڼه مومي یا لغوه کېږي. د شمالي سیمو او فدرالي پلازمېنې اسلام اباد لپاره د قانون جوړونې حق ملي شورا او سنا ته دی. مقننه په ساده اکثریت عادي قانون لغوه یا بدلولی شي.

Functions of the Legislature/Parliament in Pakistan

According to the Constitution of 1973 in Pakistan, the duties of the legislature are as follows:

1. Legislative Functions

The most important responsibility of the legislature is law-making. The constitution gives the legislature this responsibility of making laws on the list of federal subjects. The list of federal subjects (Federal Legislative List) is the list on whose subjects the National Assembly and Senate can make laws. According to the constitution, if because of some unpleasant situation the President declares a state of emergency in any province, the law-making power of the provincial assembly is suspended and the National Assembly and Senate make laws for that province. In the absence of the central assembly the President of Pakistan has the power to issue orders or ordinances, but if a session of the National Assembly and Senate begins, the President’s ordinances are either given regular legal shape or are ended. The National Assembly and Senate have the right to make laws for the Northern Areas and the federal capital Islamabad. The legislature can end or change ordinary laws by a simple majority.

مقننہ کی سب سے اہم ذمہ داری قانون سازی کرنا ہے۔ آئین مقننہ کو یہ ذمہ داری دیتا ہے کہ وفاقی اُمور کی فہرست سے قانون سازی کرے۔ وفاقی اُمور کی فہرست (Federal Legislative List) وہ فہرست ہے جس میں دیئے گئے موضوعات پر قومی اسمبلی و سینٹ قانون بنا سکتی ہے۔ آئین کے مطابق اگر کسی ناخوشگوار صورتِ حال کی وجہ سے صدرِ مملکت کسی صوبے میں ہنگامی حالت (Emergency) کا نفاذ کرے تو صوبائی اسمبلی کی قانون سازی کا اختیار معطل ہو جاتا ہے اور اُس صوبے کیلئے قومی اسمبلی و سینٹ قانون سازی کرتی ہے۔ مرکزی اسمبلی کی غیر موجودگی میں صدرِ پاکستان کو حکم نامہ یا عارضی قانون (Ordinance) جاری کرنے کا اختیار ہے لیکن اگر قومی اسمبلی و سینٹ کا اجلاس شروع ہو جائے تو صدر کے حکم ناموں کو یا تو باقاعدہ قانونی شکل دی جاتی ہے یا اسے ختم کر دیئے جاتے ہیں۔ شمالی علاقوں اور وفاقی دارالحکومت اسلام آباد کیلئے قانون سازی کا حق قومی اسمبلی و سینٹ کو حاصل ہے۔ مقننہ سادہ اکثریت سے عام قانون کو ختم یا تبدیل کر سکتی ہے۔

sections.title: باب 1 — متن (12)

paras.text: According to the constitution the Prime Minister is the executive head of the country, and his election is made by the majority of all the members of the National Assembly. The President of Pakistan is elected by Parliament (Senate + National Assembly) together with the provincial assemblies. The federal ministers (cabinet) are taken from Parliament (from the National Assembly 75 percent and from the Senate 25 percent). The Prime Minister and ministers remain in their offices as long as they enjoy the confidence of the majority of all the members of the National Assembly. The Prime Minister and ministers are answerable to Parliament. The National Assembly keeps a strict watch over the executive. The National Assembly and Senate establish control over the Prime Minister and ministers in several ways. (The members of Parliament, National Assembly and Senate, ask questions of the ministers and the ministers are bound to answer.) In Parliament the standing committees made up of members of the assembly review questions and answers. In this way the complaints of the members of the assembly are removed and a strict watch is kept on the government. Members of Parliament criticise the policies and activities of the government during the session and through the media, and do not let the government exceed its powers. Members of the legislature can stop law-making and present an Adjournment Motion for debate on any urgent national issue, and in this way this issue can be debated. The legislature can pass a resolution by consensus or majority. Although the government is not legally bound to act upon the resolution, on moral grounds it cannot ignore it either. In fact it is a recommendation to the government to do or not do some work. Members of the assembly have some privileges and rights; if these privileges and rights are harmed or any issue arises, the motion they present is called a Privilege Motion. Members of the assembly, through a Point of Order, walkout and Call Attention Notice etc., draw the government’s attention to its weaknesses and to national problems.

sections.content:
2. Executive Functions

According to the constitution the Prime Minister is the executive head of the country, and his election is made by the majority of all the members of the National Assembly. The President of Pakistan is elected by Parliament (Senate + National Assembly) together with the provincial assemblies. The federal ministers (cabinet) are taken from Parliament (from the National Assembly 75 percent and from the Senate 25 percent). The Prime Minister and ministers remain in their offices as long as they enjoy the confidence of the majority of all the members of the National Assembly. The Prime Minister and ministers are answerable to Parliament. The National Assembly keeps a strict watch over the executive. The National Assembly and Senate establish control over the Prime Minister and ministers in several ways. (The members of Parliament, National Assembly and Senate, ask questions of the ministers and the ministers are bound to answer.) In Parliament the standing committees made up of members of the assembly review questions and answers. In this way the complaints of the members of the assembly are removed and a strict watch is kept on the government. Members of Parliament criticise the policies and activities of the government during the session and through the media, and do not let the government exceed its powers. Members of the legislature can stop law-making and present an Adjournment Motion for debate on any urgent national issue, and in this way this issue can be debated. The legislature can pass a resolution by consensus or majority. Although the government is not legally bound to act upon the resolution, on moral grounds it cannot ignore it either. In fact it is a recommendation to the government to do or not do some work. Members of the assembly have some privileges and rights; if these privileges and rights are harmed or any issue arises, the motion they present is called a Privilege Motion. Members of the assembly, through a Point of Order, walkout and Call Attention Notice etc., draw the government’s attention to its weaknesses and to national problems.

3. Financial Functions
